# Tools

You may call one or more functions to assist with the user query.

You are provided with function signatures within <tools></tools> XML tags:
<tools>
{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "record_items", "description": "Record the items of an order.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"customer": {"type": "string", "description": "Who the order is for."}, "items": {"type": "array", "description": "The items ordered.", "items": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"sku": {"type": "string", "description": "The product code."}, "quantity": {"type": "integer", "description": "How many."}, "options": {"type": "array", "description": "Chosen options.", "items": {"type": "string"}}}, "required": ["sku", "quantity"]}}}, "required": ["customer", "items"]}}}
</tools>

For each function call, output the function name and arguments within the following XML format:
<tool_call>{function-name}<arg_key>{arg-key-1}</arg_key><arg_value>{arg-value-1}</arg_value><arg_key>{arg-key-2}</arg_key><arg_value>{arg-value-2}</arg_value>...</tool_call><|system|>You are a terse coding agent working in a workspace. Use the tools; do not guess file contents.<|user|>Record an order for Ada: two of SKU-1 with options gift and rush, and one SKU-9.<|assistant|><think>
